label: QSFP28 100GBASE-ER4 40 km
notes: IEEE 802.3 Clause 88 (100GBASE-ER4), per-lane averages, and the budget is the launch FLOOR minus the receive minimum: launch -2.9..+2.9 dBm against average receive power -20.9..+4.5 dBm, so -2.9 - (-20.9) = 18.0 dB over 40 km of G.652. This note used to print that same 18.0 as 2.9 - (-20.9), which is 23.8: the ceiling is not the term, and a reader who budgets 23.8 dB plans a span that cannot be lit. Clause 88's own OMA sensitivity figure is -21.4 dBm; -20.9 is the average-power minimum this engine subtracts, the same convention the LR4 and ZR4 rows use. Table 88-7 prints the ceiling as 2.9 dBm with total average launch power 8.9 dBm, against LR4's 4.5 and 10.5 - six dB between the per-lane ceiling and the total on both rows. The QSFP28 sheets split on this rung and the split matters before an order: FS's QSFP28-ER4-100G and Naddod's QSFP-100G-ER4 print 10.5 dBm and -2.9..+4.5, which is LR4's pair and not ER4's, while the CFP/CFP2 parts (Cyan 280-0409-00, Ciena 160-9115-900, Gigalight GF2-S101-ER4C) and Source Photonics' SPQ-CE-ER-CDFA print 8.9 dBm and -2.9..+2.9 like the clause. This row carries the clause, because a class row is what a budget is written against and a module above the class is a question for the module. The receive maximum is the other half of the class and it is deliberately loose: 4.5 dBm sits above ER4's own launch ceiling so an ER4 receiver still accepts an LR4 transmitter at short reach, which is why this row asks for no pad on a short span - measured, a 1 km bare run reads ok at the launch floor (-3.25 dBm at the far end, 7.75 dB under the overload point) and the top of the window reaches 2.55 dBm, still 1.95 dB inside it. Buy a module whose sheet prints a lower receive maximum and the pad comes back: FS and Naddod print -4.9 dBm, ROBOfiber's QSFP-10040-ER4 prints -3.5, and with either part any span under 2.0 dB of ODN (5.7 km at 0.35 dB/km) overdrives the far end while this row, read at its own 4.5, calls the same span ok. The margin is the tighter verdict even on the class's figures, and it is measured: 40 km x 0.35 = 14.0 dB of the 18.0 leaves 4.0 dB and reads MARGINAL rather than ok, because ok needs margin + 2; ten fusion splices at 0.1 dB leave 3.0 dB and it is still marginal, at the default margin exactly; two SC/APC matings at 0.3 dB leave 2.4 dB and it fails on headroom, naming sensitivity -20.9 dBm. A 40 km ER4 link is a spliced plant, not a patched one. ER4 transmits over four LAN-WDM lanes (1294.53-1296.59, 1299.02-1301.09, 1303.54-1305.63, 1308.09-1310.19 nm) and this engine budgets one wavelength, so the row says 1310 nm - the top lane and the window the cables publish 0.35 dB/km for; the per-lane figures are the worst-lane ones, so the single-wavelength budget errs conservative. Class figures, not one measured module: replace the row with the part actually purchased before pricing a build.
